docMeta.dd: Chapter 40, The Valley of the Shadow

source.excerpt: You must take my place, Jo, and be everything to Father and Mother when I’m gone. They will turn to you, don’t fail them, and if it’s hard to work alone, remember that I don’t forget you, and that you’ll be happier in doing that than writing splendid books or seeing all the world, for love is the only thing that we can carry with us when we go, and it makes the end so easy.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Beth asks Jo to care for their parents after her death. The familiar quotation extracts the final clause of this farewell, so it should be credited to Alcott’s fictional dialogue rather than to an autobiographical deathbed remark.
